title: A title's size is a number you type or nudge, the way the title mock draws it
goal: The title mock gives a title's Text section a Size box you type a number into, sitting beside the Weight dropdown, the way Photoshop's size field takes any number. The app offers Size as a dropdown of seven preset sizes on its own row, so a size between the presets can only be reached by dragging the box on the canvas. Build the mock's Size box, keeping the presets reachable.
notes: Mock: docs/design/mocks/pages/video-title-wt.html line ~214, .numgrid with Size beside Regular. App: TextInspector.swift SelectionMenu(label: "Size") over TextStyles.fontSizes, now on VideoKit.Dropdown (2026-10-05, the-text-section-s-font-size-and-weight-menus-lo); CaptionsInspector.swift CaptionsTextInspector has the same Size row. Seen in queue/audits/2026-10-05-text-menus-after-dark-sc.png. The panel-rows-in-one-column layout stacks Size and Weight as two rows (PanelPair); the mock puts them side by side on one line, so the runner decides with the placement contract whether the pair shares a row. Size is clamped by setTextStyle already (typed sizes in walks use setTextSizeThreeDigits).
acceptance: With a title picked at Next defaults, the Text section shows Size as a box you can type a number into, beside Weight, as video-title-wt.html draws it (stepper sm with Size in it)
Typing a size and pressing Return changes every picked text in one undo step; Mixed still reads Mixed in the dimmed style
The preset sizes stay one click away (arrow keys nudge, or a preset list on the box), and the Captions layer's Size row gets the same control
A walk types a size and photographs the section beside the mock frame, light and dark
